bug_found.discovered_via: this phase's own real container install/doctor validation (Section 26) -- not present in Phase 28's own testing, which only ever ran --doctor on a host with a real GPU
bug_found.root_cause: llama_supports_gpu_offload() (third_party/llama.cpp/src/llama.cpp) checks for an actually-ENUMERATED GPU/IGPU ggml_backend device, not whether a GPU backend was compiled into the binary -- confirmed by reading the upstream source directly. A Vulkan-enabled build with zero visible devices at runtime (this phase's container: libvulkan1 + mesa-vulkan-drivers installed, but no /dev/dri passthrough) therefore reports the SAME false value as a build with no GPU backend compiled in at all.
bug_found.prior_behavior: tools/membrane-run/main.cpp's run_doctor_mode() (introduced in Phase 28) asserted "[WARN] no GPU backend compiled in (CPU-only build -- rebuild with e.g. -DGGML_VULKAN=ON for GPU offload)" whenever this conflated check was false -- false and actively misleading advice on an already-Vulkan-enabled build, as proven directly above (local_host_reference_check shows the SAME binary correctly finds 2 GPU devices with real hardware present).
bug_found.fix: run_doctor_mode() no longer asserts a specific unverifiable cause: both real causes (no backend compiled in vs. backend compiled in but 0 devices found) now share one honest combined [WARN] message. Scoped strictly to this phase's own --doctor presentation code (introduced last phase, owned by this project's CLI layer) -- the underlying resolve_gpu_config()/--gpu-layers auto planner code path (Phase 9B.1, pre-existing, out of this phase's no-planner-changes scope) was left untouched.
bug_found.status: fixed in this phase's commit, verified with the same real container reproduction both before and after the fix
